items.stem: Define the term 'inventory'.
items.answer: Stocks of raw materials, work in progress and finished goods held by a business.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – Stocks of raw materials, work in progress and finished goods held by a business. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two costs of holding large amounts of inventory.
items.answer: Storage costs such as warehouse rent and insurance; and the opportunity cost of cash tied up that could be used elsewhere, plus the risk of goods becoming obsolete or damaged.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark cost, 1 mark explanation): storage, opportunity cost, obsolescence, damage/theft. [4]

items.stem: Explain why a business holds inventory of finished goods.
items.answer: To meet unexpected increases in demand and fill orders quickly, so it does not lose sales to competitors.
items.markingKey: 1 mark meet demand/unexpected orders; 1 mark avoid lost sales. [2]

items.stem: Based in Kuala Lumpur, BatikPay Sdn Bhd (private limited company) runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops. The business has around 210 employees. The central bank has announced tighter rules on data protection for payment apps. Explain the problems BatikPay could face if it holds too little inventory.
items.answer: Points to develop for BatikPay: low inventory risks stock-outs; lost sales and customer goodwill; production stops if materials run out; higher ordering costs from frequent small orders.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: low inventory risks stock-outs. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to BatikPay (financial technology). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. lost sales and customer goodwill; production stops if materials run out. [3]

items.stem: Cape Brew Co. (Pty) Ltd is a private limited company based in Cape Town, South Africa. It brews craft beers and low-sugar soft drinks sold through bars and supermarkets and employs about 140 people. Demand has grown faster than its small brewery can produce. Explain the problems Cape Brew could face if it holds too little inventory.
items.answer: Points to develop for Cape Brew: low inventory risks stock-outs; lost sales and customer goodwill; production stops if materials run out; higher ordering costs from frequent small orders.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: low inventory risks stock-outs. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Cape Brew (beverages). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. lost sales and customer goodwill; production stops if materials run out. [3]

items.stem: Andes Textil SA is a family-owned private company based in Lima, Peru. It makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan and employs about 320 people. The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Evaluate how Andes Textil should decide how much inventory to hold.
items.answer: For: avoid stock-outs; meet seasonal demand; bulk discounts. Against: storage and opportunity costs; obsolescence; cash-flow pressure. Judgement: for Andes Textil it depends mainly on how predictable demand is, and also on supplier reliability.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [2]: relevant concepts. AO2 Application [2]: uses the evidence (Andes Textil: textile manufacturing, about 320 employees, family-owned private company in Peru; the founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production). AO3 Analysis [3]: arguments for, e.g. avoid stock-outs; meet seasonal demand; bulk discounts; arguments against, e.g. storage and opportunity costs; obsolescence; cash-flow pressure. AO4 Evaluation [3]: a justified judgement that weighs the arguments, e.g. it depends on how predictable demand is; supplier reliability; the nature of alpaca knitwear. A top-level answer reaches a supported conclusion specific to Andes Textil. [10]

Idle production lines due to shortages

items.stem: Define the term 'buffer inventory'.
items.answer: The minimum level of inventory held to avoid running out if deliveries are late or demand is higher than expected.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – The minimum level of inventory held to avoid running out if deliveries are late or demand is higher than expected. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business holds buffer inventory.
items.answer: In case a delivery is late or demand is higher than expected, so it can keep producing and selling without a stock-out.
items.markingKey: 1 mark late deliveries/unexpected demand; 1 mark avoids stock-outs. [2]

items.stem: Explain one limitation of an inventory control chart.
items.answer: It assumes inventory is used at a constant rate and that lead times are fixed, but demand and delivery times vary in reality.
items.markingKey: 1 mark limitation; 1 mark explanation. [2]

items.stem: Nusantara Apparel is a public limited company in Jakarta, Indonesia with about 4,000 staff. It makes sportswear under contract for global brands. items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: the chart shows maximum, reorder and buffer levels; orders placed at the reorder level; buffer inventory protects against delays; reduces both stock-outs and excess inventory.

items.stem: Define the term 'just-in-time (JIT)'.
items.answer: An inventory management system in which materials are delivered just when they are needed for production, so little or no buffer inventory is held.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: full definition – An inventory management system in which materials are delivered just when they are needed for production, so little or no buffer inventory is held. 1 mark: partial definition or a relevant example only. [2]

items.stem: Explain two disadvantages of using JIT.
items.answer: If a supplier delivers late, production stops because there is no buffer inventory; and frequent small deliveries lose bulk-buying discounts and raise ordering and transport costs.
items.markingKey: 2 × (1 mark disadvantage, 1 mark explanation). [4]

items.stem: Explain why JIT can improve a business's cash flow.
items.answer: Less cash is spent on inventory before it is needed, so more cash is available for other uses and storage costs fall.
items.markingKey: 1 mark less cash tied up in inventory; 1 mark lower storage costs/other uses. [2]

items.stem: Tanvir Textiles Ltd is a private limited company based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It makes shirts and T-shirts for European fashion retailers and employs about 420 people. Labour turnover among machinists has risen sharply this year. Explain the benefits to Tanvir Textiles of introducing just-in-time inventory management.
items.answer: Points to develop for Tanvir Textiles: JIT means materials arrive just when needed; lower storage and insurance costs; less cash tied up in inventory; less waste and obsolescence.
items.markingKey: AO1 Knowledge [1]: JIT means materials arrive just when needed. AO2 Application [1]: point linked to Tanvir Textiles (clothing manufacturing). AO3 Analysis [1]: developed explanation of the consequence, e.g. lower storage and insurance costs; less cash tied up in inventory. [3]

The level of inventory at which a new order is placed.
An approach to production that aims to minimise waste of all resources, including time, materials and inventory.
The time between placing an order with a supplier and receiving the delivery.
items.answer: The time between placing an order with a supplier and receiving the delivery.
items.markingKey: lead time: The time between placing an order with a supplier and receiving the delivery. [1]

items.stem: Based in Mumbai, Deccan Auto Components Ltd (public limited company) supplies brakes and steering parts to car manufacturers. The business has around 2,200 employees. Its car-maker customers are switching rapidly to electric vehicles. Explain one advantage to Deccan Auto of increasing its buffer inventory.
items.answer: Fewer stock-outs; this would help Deccan Auto, which supplies brakes and steering parts to car manufacturers.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: relevant advantage, e.g. fewer stock-outs; can meet unexpected demand; protection against late deliveries. 1 mark: explained in the context of Deccan Auto (automotive components). [2]

items.stem: Indus Sports uses 300 units of a component each day. The supplier's lead time is 7 days. Indus Sports keeps a buffer inventory of 1,320 units and orders 6,550 units each time. The owner set the reorder level at 2,100 units. Explain why this is wrong and calculate the correct reorder level.
items.answer: The buffer inventory was not added to usage during the lead time. Correct reorder level: 3,420 units.
items.markingKey: Error explained: the buffer inventory was not added to usage during the lead time [1]; working: 1,320 + 300 × 7 [1]; correct reorder level: 3,420 units [1] [3]

items.answer: 3,680 units

items.stem: Kiwi Trails is a private limited company in Auckland, New Zealand with about 90 staff. It runs guided hiking, kayaking and cycling tours. Bookings are highly seasonal and most guides are employed only for the summer. Explain how an inventory control chart could help Kiwi Trails manage its inventory.
items.answer: Points to develop for Kiwi Trails: the chart shows maximum, reorder and buffer levels; orders placed at the reorder level; buffer inventory protects against delays; reduces both stock-outs and excess inventory.

items.stem: The founder is retiring and the new managing director wants to modernise production. Andes Textil SA, a family-owned private company in Peru with about 320 employees, makes premium alpaca knitwear for fashion retailers in North America and Japan. (a) Analyse how an inventory control chart could help Andes Textil manage its inventory. (b) Evaluate whether Andes Textil should increase its buffer inventory after recent late deliveries from suppliers.
items.answer: (a) The chart shows maximum, reorder and buffer levels; orders placed at the reorder level; buffer inventory protects against delays; reduces both stock-outs and excess inventory. (b) For: avoids stock-outs; protects customer goodwill; continuous production. Against: higher holding costs; cash tied up; better to find reliable suppliers. Judgement: for Andes Textil it depends mainly on how often deliveries are late, and also on the cost of a stock-out.

items.stem: Based in Kuala Lumpur, BatikPay Sdn Bhd (private limited company) runs a mobile payments app used by 4 million customers and 90 000 small shops. The business has around 210 employees. items.stem: Nusantara Apparel Tbk is a public limited company based in Jakarta, Indonesia. It makes sportswear under contract for global brands and employs about 4,000 people. A global brand has threatened to cancel its contract after a report on long working hours. Explain the benefits to Nusantara Apparel of introducing just-in-time inventory management.
items.answer: Points to develop for Nusantara Apparel: JIT means materials arrive just when needed; lower storage and insurance costs; less cash tied up in inventory; less waste and obsolescence.
